Calculate the number-average molecular weight (Mn) of a polymer sample.
The molecular-weight distribution is given as four molecular weights with their corresponding number of chains (counts): 56526 g/mol (96 chains), 92809 g/mol (131 chains), 115856 g/mol (153 chains), and 126029 g/mol (146 chains).
Use the definition Mn = Σ(Ni · Mi) / Σ(Ni).
Interpret each value in parentheses as the number of molecules (Ni) at that molecular weight (Mi).
Compute Σ(Ni · Mi) = 56526×96 + 92809×131 + 115856×153 + 126029×146 = 53,710,677 g/mol·chains.
Compute Σ(Ni) = 96 + 131 + 153 + 146 = 526 chains.
Divide: Mn = 53,710,677 / 526 ≈ 102,112 g/mol.
Report the final answer as Mn ≈ 102,112 g/mol (approximately 1.02 × 10^5 g/mol).
